1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18	
19	At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution.
22

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection. Tripping that device removes every charging session on the branch at once, and in many installations it also removes the auxiliary loads sharing the branch.
4	
5	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
6	
7	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
8	
9	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

findings.title: Detailed description says the branch current limit is received over the network interface, which the disclosure does not state and which contradicts the same section's own definition of that limit
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 37 (and paragraph at line 1)
findings.detail: The disclosure confines the network interface to remote schedules and authorizations: "The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory." It never says the branch limit itself arrives over the network. The candidate adds that origin, and the addition collides with the candidate's own opening definition of the branch current limit as a physical property of the installation. As written the document gives the branch current limit two mutually exclusive sources — the conductor/overcurrent-device/supply rating in paragraph 1, and a value most recently received over the network in paragraph 37 — and the reader cannot tell which quantity claims 1, 9, 14 and 18 allocate against. Note that the summary (draft/06-summary.md line 9) and claims 9 and 18 stay neutral ("to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory"), so the unsupported assertion is local to this paragraph and can be removed without disturbing the claims. Paragraph 1's list of what fixes the limit ("by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity") is likewise not in the disclosure, which says only "one electrical branch whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings"; the two passages together are what produce the contradiction.

findings.title: In FIG. 4 the leaders for 212, 214 and 216 terminate on the connector arrows outside their shapes, so 214 lands on shape 212 and 216 lands on shape 214
findings.detail: I re-opened figures/rendered-FIG-4.png (sha256 5df5c705... , matching review/figure-audit-evidence.json). Reading down the column, the shapes are rect 202, rect 204, rect 206, rect 208, diamond 210, rect 212, diamond 214, rect 216, and eight terminal dots sit on the column's vertical centre line. Dots 2, 3 and 4 lie inside rect 204, rect 206 and rect 208 respectively. The remaining dots do not: the dot reached by the 212 leader sits on the vertical arrow in the white gap between the lower vertex of diamond 210 and the top edge of rect 212, touching neither; the dot reached by the 214 leader sits on the lower edge of rect 212, a full arrow-length above the upper vertex of diamond 214; and the dot reached by the 216 leader sits on the lower vertex of diamond 214, a full arrow-length above the top edge of rect 216. Rect 212, diamond 214 and rect 216 each have a completely empty interior with no dot in it, which is directly visible in the render. The consequence is that numeral 214 (welded-contactor isolation step) terminates on the geometry of the ordered shedding step and numeral 216 (conditional reclosure step) terminates on the geometry of the welded-contactor isolation step, so two numerals designate a part other than the one the ledger and the detailed description assign to them. The 210 dot likewise sits at/just above the upper vertex of diamond 210 rather than well inside it. The recorded endpoint evidence marks all eight 'correct', but for FIG. 4 its per-label evidence strings are content-free restatements of the target ('Terminal dot is correctly placed on the visible welded-contactor isolation step geometry') with no coordinates, unlike the FIG. 2 entries which give native pixel positions; it therefore records no pixel relationship that contradicts what the image shows.

findings.title: In FIG. 2 numeral 108 (isolated local bus) terminates on the dashed sensing-connection line, which the same brief calls a connection separate from the bus
findings.where: figures/rendered-FIG-2.png and figures/FIG-2.md, numeral list entry for 108
findings.detail: I re-opened figures/rendered-FIG-2.png (sha256 dcc6c764..., matching the evidence file). In the lower left of the sheet there are two distinct horizontal runs entering from the left edge: a thick SOLID line at the control-pilot interface height, which crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle and continues right to the left side of the control-pilot block — this is the isolated local bus — and, clearly below it with white space between, a thick DASHED run that comes in from the left edge, turns at a bend inside the dashed rectangle and rises diagonally to the bottom of the connector current sensor circle — this is the sensing-connection line. The 108 leader rises from the numeral at the bottom-left and its terminal dot sits exactly on the bend of the dashed run, inside the dashed rectangle, not on the solid bus line and not left of the dashed rectangle. The recorded endpoint evidence is self-contradicting on this point: it states the dot is "on the dashed line representing the isolated local bus geometry", but FIG-2.md specifies the isolated local bus as a solid line and the only dashed line work in the figure is the channel enclosure 120 and the sensing connection. The check therefore matched the dot to a dashed line that the brief expressly identifies as a different element. As drawn, numeral 108 labels the sensor sensing connection, and the detailed description's statement that the bus carries the contactor commands and pilot reports is not the thing the numeral points at.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-2.md: "- 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the bus line left of the dashed rectangle." and "A dashed sensing-connection line runs from the lower part of the circle outline of the connector current sensor down and to the left, exiting the dashed rectangle on the left side, indicating a connection to the edge controller separate from the isolated local bus." review/figure-audit-evidence.json, FIG. 2: "numeral": "108", "correct": true, "evidence": "The terminal dot is located at (276, 690), which is on the dashed line representing the isolated local bus geometry."
findings.fix: Regenerate FIG. 2 with the 108 leader terminating on the solid bus line in the portion that lies left of the dashed rectangle, and tighten the brief entry to "- 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the solid bus line in the portion between the left edge of the drawing area and the left side of the dashed rectangle, clear of the dashed sensing-connection line."

findings.title: In FIG. 2 the leader for 128 runs through the interior of the electric vehicle 130 and crosses its outline twice
findings.where: figures/rendered-FIG-2.png and figures/FIG-2.md, numeral list entry for 128
findings.detail: In the rendered sheet, the numeral 128 sits at the far bottom-right of the drawing area and its leader is a long diagonal running up and to the left across roughly half the sheet width. On its way it enters the rounded rectangle representing the electric vehicle 130 through the lower part of that outline, passes across the interior of 130, exits through the left side of the rounded rectangle, and only then reaches the vehicle connector block, entering it through its right edge and terminating on a dot near the top of that block. The leader therefore crosses the outline of a different, separately numbered element twice and traverses its interior, contrary to the brief's own rule that each leader be short and clear of the line work, and it leaves the reader to decide by eye whether 128 designates the block or the vehicle it passes through. The audit evidence records only the terminal dot position for 128 and 130; it does not assess the leader's path, so it is silent on this defect rather than contradicting it.

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows a full-width solid horizontal line near the bottom of the installation enclosure that the brief does not describe and no numeral identifies
findings.where: figures/rendered-FIG-1.png, lower portion of the dashed enclosure; figures/FIG-1.md
findings.detail: I opened figures/rendered-FIG-1.png twice (sha256 591cd51a..., matching the evidence file). Below the edge controller block and above the dashed bottom side of the enclosure there is a continuous SOLID horizontal line, plainly separated from the dashed bottom side by a band of white paper, running the whole way from the left dashed side of the enclosure to the right dashed side. FIG-1.md enumerates the figure's line work exhaustively — enclosure, branch conductor, sensor rectangle, three vertical drops, three blocks, the edge controller block, the isolated local bus with its two rising branches, and the dashed sensing connection — and this line is none of them: it is far below the bus line, extends well to the right of the bus's stated right-hand end beneath the middle block, and carries no reference numeral. In an electrical schematic an unexplained conductor-like line spanning the whole installation reads as an additional connection that neither the disclosure nor the detailed description provides. The recorded geometry check reports "no unexpected elements", but it is a prose summary with an empty "unexpected" array and records no pixel measurement of the enclosure's lower region, so it does not account for this line. I am confident the line is present and unnumbered; I could not determine from pixels alone whether it originates as a duplicated enclosure border or as spurious geometry, and I say so.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-1.md: "A flat schematic system diagram in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words other than the reference numerals listed below." — "A solid line leaves the right side of the edge controller block and runs horizontally beneath the leftmost block and the middle block as an isolated local bus, its right end stopping beneath the middle block and well to the left of the rightmost block." review/figure-audit-evidence.json, FIG. 1: "summary": "The drawing perfectly matches the specification. findings.where: figures/rendered-FIG-1.png; figures/FIG-1.md, numeral list entry for 106
findings.detail: In the render, the dashed sensing-connection line descends from the branch current sensor rectangle and terminates on the top side of the edge controller block, and the terminal dot of the 106 leader sits at essentially that same point on the top side rather than well inside the block. A leader ending on the outline of the correct element is acceptable practice, so the numeral is not pointing at the wrong part; the defect is that its endpoint is superimposed on another line's terminus, which makes it read as though it could designate the dashed connection. My reading here rests on visual estimation of a few pixels of separation, so I mark it minor; the recorded endpoint evidence describes the dot as "inside the rectangular box", which is consistent with a dot lying just within the top edge.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-1.md: "- 106 edge controller: leader ends well inside the lower left block." and "A dashed sensing-connection line runs from the bottom side of the branch current sensor rectangle down and left to the top side of the edge controller block."
findings.fix: Tighten the FIG-1.md entry to "- 106 edge controller: leader ends in the interior of the lower left block, in its lower right quadrant, clear of the block outline and clear of the point at which the dashed sensing-connection line meets the block", and regenerate the sheet.

The controller/edge-controller naming is expressly bridged ("An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller"), "connector channel" is used consistently across claims, description and numeral ledger, and the definitional glosses (minimum sustaining current, safety reserve, leakage threshold, stored shedding order, energy-deficit value) stay neutral rather than adding undisclosed mechanism.
